name: Lee Sin
notes: Casts go one after another: Dragon's Rage (R) opens at t=0 and keeps Lee Sin busy for its 0.25 s cast time; Sonic Wave (Q1) follows once that ends and is busy for its own 0.25 s; Resonating Strike (Q2, the wiki's 'cast time: none') recasts the instant the mark exists and only holds the next attack back 0.25 s as a dash; Tempest (E) then takes its own 0.25 s cast time. No two casts land in the same instant.

Resonating Strike (Q2) is recast the instant Sonic Wave lands rather than being held to the end of its 3 s window for a bigger missing-health bonus: the dossier's proposed rotation calls for recasting it 'as soon as it lands', and later Q cycles in the fight naturally see more missing health as the dummy's HP drops, so total damage still only rises over time.
Iron Will/Safeguard (W) is never cast: neither half deals damage to the dummy, so it would only cost cast time for a defensive effect the fight doesn't need.
Cripple (E's second half) is never cast: it is a slow with no damage component, so casting it only burns a global window that could otherwise go to Tempest/Sonic Wave/attacks.

Flurry (P) is treated as arming on every damaging cast (Q1, Q2, E, R alike): the next 2 attacks that land within its 3 s window get +40% bonus attack speed; no on-hit damage or energy is modeled since energy is not simulated by the engine.
Dragon's Rage only deals its primary-target damage: the collision bonus against a second body requires another unit, which never exists in a 1v1 dummy fight.
None of Lee Sin's ability damage is flagged as able to critically strike by the wiki, so all ability hits are dealt with crit_mod = false.

Energy costs are not modeled: nothing in this kit binds a level-16 Lee Sin's rotation inside a 15 s fight once Flurry's own energy return is accounted for, per the engine's guidance to only track a resource pool if it would really stop casts.

assumed.why: Flurry's own 'empowered attacks must land within a short time' window isn't separately binned; using the 3 s recast window shared by Q/W/E's own reactivation timers, the only 3-second constant the dossier could tie to it.
